clue.text: Powerful figure in grip of drug

indicators.note: something in the grip of another is held inside it, so the number goes within the drug word

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis
ten is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: A strong person is caught up in drug use.
explanation.definitionFit: A potent force is a powerful one; the words are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Suggest showing professional attitude

parts.note: pro is the short form of professional
a pose is a bodily attitude or posture

explanation.surface: Someone hints at their professional manner.
explanation.definitionFit: To propose an idea is to suggest it; a plain synonym.

clue.text: Centre of nest remains as orifice

indicators.note: the letters sit in the middle of the run of words, straddling the gap between them

explanation.surface: What is left in the middle of a bird's nest serves as a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre of' points to letters inside the phrase 'nest remains', not just the middle of 'nest'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trema is a zoological term for an opening or perforation, an orifice in an organism.

clue.text: Small boys with pincers

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both young children in slang and claws or gripping pincers.

clue.text: Jesting at one attempting to slim

definitions.meaning: to bant was to follow William Banting's diet, so a dieter is one who bants

explanation.walkthrough: To 'bant' is an old verb from William Banting's Victorian slimming diet; someone who does it is a 'banter'.
explanation.definitionFit: Banter is light jesting talk; the second sense is a whimsical agent noun from the old verb bant, to diet.

clue.text: Attribute certain qualities to a writer

parts.note: a scribe is one who writes

explanation.surface: Someone credits an author with certain qualities.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascribe is to attribute something, such as a quality, to a person.

clue.text: Conduct orchestral rehearsals for the militia

definitions.meaning: to train a band is to rehearse an orchestra
... were citizen militia companies of 16th-17th century London

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means coaching a band; as one it is the historical name for London's civic militia.

clue.text: Renounces former creed and is able to throw rest out

indicators.note: the scrambled letters sit out around the other piece, holding it inside
to throw the word rest is to scatter its letters into a new order

parts.note: can means is able to

explanation.surface: A convert gives up old beliefs and can cast away rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Renounces former creed' is the whole definition; 'throw' signals the scramble, and 'out' means its letters stand outside the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To recant is to withdraw formally a belief once held, renouncing it.

clue.text: Force the Spanish to follow competition

indicators.note: the article comes after the contest word, following it in the answer

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Someone forces the Spanish to come behind in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: To compel is to force someone to act; a direct synonym.

clue.text: Surface with Scotch tar mixture to meet a requirement

parts.note: to surface is to come up from below

indicators.note: a mixture of the two words blends their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A road is resurfaced with a blend of Scottish tar to meet the specification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixture' rearranges SCOTCH TAR into TO SCRATCH.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to reach the required standard, from the line or scratch athletes had to start at.

clue.text: Did poor mad Poe put this on top?

definitions.text: Did poor mad Poe put this on top?

indicators.note: poor suggests the words are in a sorry, disordered state, so their letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A question whether the troubled writer Edgar Allan Poe greased his hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges MAD POE; the whole clue also asks what one puts on one's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomade is a scented hair ointment, something applied on top of the head.

clue.text: Moving point wounded nag internally

indicators.note: the scrambled horse word goes inside, internally, the other word
wounded suggests damage, so the letters of nag are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A touching moment when a sharp point injures a horse inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' looks like movement, but it means emotionally stirring; 'wounded' is the anagram signal and 'internally' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Something poignant is emotionally moving, touching the feelings.

clue.text: Always taking right girl out, even in defeat

parts.note: ever means always, as in for ever
Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally or Sarah

explanation.surface: Even when beaten, someone keeps taking a girl out on dates.
explanation.definitionFit: A reversal is a setback or defeat, a turn of fortune for the worse.

clue.text: It uplifts one to find oracles at work

indicators.note: set to work, the letters are reorganised into a new word

explanation.surface: Something raises a person to visit prophets at their labours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges ORACLES AT; 'to find' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A moving staircase carries people upwards, a cryptic way of describing it.

clue.text: Slip away to see pal, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks off to visit a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that elapses slips away or passes by.

clue.text: Soldier's vehicle turned over to draughtsman

indicators.note: turned over means the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for soldiers; the possessive adds no letter
a cart is a simple vehicle

explanation.surface: A soldier hands over his wagon to a technical drawer.
explanation.walkthrough: RE plus CART gives RECART, which 'turned over' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A tracer is one who traces drawings, a kind of draughtsman copying plans.

clue.text: Attains goal, but feels those pains again

definitions.meaning: to reach a destination is to attain it

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both arrives at a goal and, split as re-aches, aches a second time.

clue.text: Frenchman brought up law's restoration

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter; law is rule

explanation.surface: A Frenchman raised the restoration of the law.
explanation.definitionFit: A renewal is a restoring of something to a fresh state.

clue.text: Obliterated when we do it up carelessly

indicators.note: doing something carelessly leaves the letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone wiped things out by doing up a job sloppily.
explanation.definitionFit: Wiped out means destroyed entirely, obliterated.

clue.text: Turned aside to take in female by boat

indicators.note: the outer word takes in the other, holding it inside

parts.note: wry once meant twisted or turned aside
her is a female pronoun

explanation.surface: A vessel swerved to pick up a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A wherry is a light rowing boat or barge.

clue.text: Becomes engaged in predicaments

definitions.meaning: to plight one's troth is to pledge to marry

explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense is pledges in betrothal; the noun is a bad situation or predicament.

clue.text: Note unusual lines of vessel

parts.note: ut is the old name for the note doh in sol-fa

indicators.note: an unusual arrangement of the word lines shuffles its letters

explanation.surface: Unusual lines of a ship are worth noting.
explanation.definitionFit: A utensil is a household container or tool; a vessel in the sense of a pot or dish.

clue.text: Standard weapon in conversation

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
a lance is a long spear

explanation.surface: A regulation weapon is mentioned in talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlance is a manner of speaking, the kind of talk used in conversation.

clue.text: Publishes points in dispute

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means puts out in print; the noun means matters under debate.

clue.text: Express derision at meal

definitions.meaning: to ... at something is to mock it
British slang for food or a meal

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to mock; in British slang the noun is food eaten greedily.

clue.text: Talks with couturier before audience at stately home

parts.note: chats are informal talks
Charles Frederick Worth was a famous 19th-century fashion designer
a theatre audience is called the house

explanation.surface: A fashion designer gives talks to a crowd at a grand country estate.
explanation.walkthrough: Chatsworth House is a famous stately home in Derbyshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Chatsworth is one of England's grandest country houses, a classic example of a stately home.

clue.text: Way to go on gentle walk

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
to roll is to go on, proceed steadily

explanation.surface: A suggested route for a gentle walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroll is a leisurely, unhurried walk.

clue.text: Advantageous to America to order fuel

parts.note: US is short for the United States of America

indicators.note: putting the letters of fuel in order rearranges them

explanation.surface: It benefits the US to place an order for fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Something useful is of benefit, advantageous.
